_about: Every parameter and decision flag for the contents replication pack. Python and R both read this file. Decision flags mirror audit/DECISIONS.md: 'signed_off' stays false until a named person approves the decision there.

source._path_note: {user} is filled in at run time from the logged-in Databricks user, so no personal details are stored here.

D03_target_definition.note: Target = incurred - recoveries, repudiated and out-of-period claims excluded. The ~3% IBNR uplift is estimated in sql/04 but NOT applied to the target.

D06_missing_as_level.note: Implemented in sql/08 only; imputation is not implemented, so apply=false is rejected.

D07_expected_claims_basis.note: Models use a log-exposure offset; earned premium (= annual written premium x exposure) is used for loss ratios and A/E only. Chosen by Gerard Murphy in session 2026-10-20.

D10_develop_ibnr.note: Three-line run only (sql/10): every reported claim grossed up by 1/F(age), F the cost-weighted report-lag distribution by line and peril. The GLM pack (run_all.py) is unchanged.

D11_ibner_motor_bi.note: Motor bodily injury only: each loss year lifted to the 2021 claim size of claims reported within 90 days, no inflation (lower bound).

D12_cap_large_claims.note: Developed claims capped at sql_variables.large_claim_cap; the line's excess is spread back as a multiplicative loading. Added during the run (A15), not in the approved plan.

D19_dedupe_claims.note: Keep one copy of claims identical on every field except claim_id (604 claims, all lines; A18). Found by the data workstream (GitHub #55) and adopted here.

D17_bf_slow_perils.note: Bornhuetter-Ferguson instead of the chain ladder for a loss year with under bf_max_reported_share of its cost reported (2024 subsidence and motor bodily injury); prior from the preceding mature years, no trend.

D26_r11_elevation_feet.note: Region R11 elevation is recorded in feet; converted to metres in addresses_clean, raw value kept (A27, A28; #154).

D27_year_built_placeholder.note: year_built = 1900 is a placeholder; replaced by the typical year built for the address's energy rating, raw value kept (A27, A28; #155).

D24_merge_timber.note: Buildings construction_type T (2021-22) and W (2023 onwards, every 2025 row) are the same timber category recoded; merged as 'timber', raw value kept (A24). Found by the data workstream (Cian, R4).

D13_trend_to_2025.note: Log-linear calendar-year trend per line, fitted jointly with XGBoost by backfitting the year term into the offset, projected to the 2025 rows. Approved by Gerard Murphy in session 2026-10-21.

oneway._note: One-way tables cover every factor, including those excluded from modelling (D-04, D-05), so the leakage stays visible.

model._alpha_note: L2 penalty (intercept unpenalised) on the scale of scikit-learn's GLM objective: (1/(2 sum w)) sum w d + alpha/2 ||b||^2. R/run_all.R minimises the same objective with its own penalised IRLS.

xgboost._about: python/run_xgb.py (audit A13). Tweedie power, fit and score years come from 'model'. Tuning never sees the score year: each grid point is fitted on years up to tune_fit_year_max and early-stopped on tune_val_year; the best is refitted on all fit years with the same number of trees and scored once.
xgboost._grid_note: min_child_weight is a hessian sum; at the base rate the Tweedie hessian is about 5 per row (median), so 2000 and 20000 mean leaves of roughly 400 and 4000 rows. Run 1 used depth 2-6 and weights 10-200, and its best point sat on the grid edge (audit A13).

banded._note: The GLM's inputs: model.factors as categoricals plus model.numeric.

raw._note: Permitted columns at full resolution (D-08). Excluded: IDs, surname, dates, date_of_birth (duplicates age), yr (trees cannot extrapolate a trend), contacts (D-04), written and earned premium (D-05), renewal_decision and all claim columns.

lines._about: python/run_lines.py (audit A15). XGBoost per line on the developed, capped target, with a backfitted log-linear year trend (D-13) and the large-claim loading (D-12). Same protocol as A13: tune on 2021-22 early-stopped on 2023; backtest fit 2021-23, score 2024; final fit 2021-24, predict 2025. Boosting settings (eta, subsampling, seed, threads, rounds) come from 'xgboost'.
lines._min_child_note: min_child_weight = rows x the line's median Tweedie hessian per row at the base rate, so leaf sizes mean the same thing on every line. Run 1 stopped at 5000 and motor's best sat on that edge (A15), so 20000 and 50000 were added.

contents._note: The banded set (model.factors and model.numeric), which beat the raw set in A13.

glm_lines._about: python/run_glm_lines.py (audit A16). Owner's design, 2026-10-22: contents one GLM (no split); buildings small claims XGBoost at depth 3 plus a large-claim GLM; motor small-claim GLM plus a large-claim GLM. Claim history (sql/12, sql/13) enters every line as a credibility factor (k + n) / (k + E), E from a frequency GLM without history, k tuned on 2023 per group. Large claims: cost above the threshold, developed, modelled by a compact Tweedie GLM and scaled to a generalised Pareto mean. Same protocol and development as A15; the D-12 cap is not used.

cann._about: A20. CANN correction of each line's small-claim model, adopted per line only if it improves both 2023 and 2024. Architecture fixed in advance, not tuned.
cann._d23: D-23 (A22): a discretionary addition, so it must also have a significant two-year mean gain (approximate 95% interval from the yearly paired bootstraps).

level._about: A20. Deviance-optimal level factor per line, adopted only if each year's factor improves the other year; then the uncertainty premium exp(sigma^2/2).

buildings._a16_note: a16_override: the A16 settings, used only for the 'no A17 changes' significance variant.

contents._seasonal_note: D-22 (A22): exposure is days weighted by the month's relative claim frequency, estimated on each window's fitting years; plain exposure is kept for reported rates.
contents._a16_note: a16_override: the A16 settings, used only for the 'no A17 changes' significance variant.
contents._smooth_note: A17: GLM A's age, elevation and river-distance bands replaced by cubic splines on the raw values (+0.0011 D2 on 2023, +0.0019 on 2024).

motor._smooth_note: A17: numerics as cubic splines, plus missed payments and credit band (+0.0053 D2 on 2023, +0.0023 on 2024). The large-claim GLM stays banded: smoothing it failed on 2023.
motor._a16_note: a16_override: the A16 settings, used only for the 'no A17 changes' significance variant.
motor._factor_note: Features with at least 1% XGBoost gain in A15.

submission._about: python/make_submission.py. Contents rows are predicted by each model refitted on every training year; rows of other lines get other_lines_value (owner's instruction, 2026-10-21). No trend or IBNR adjustment is applied (A13).

xgb_banded._source: Chosen by tuning in A13 run 2 (evidence/xgboost/ev_x1_split_test.csv).

reconcile._quasi_separation_note: Coefficients beyond +/-8 (relativity below ~3e-4 or above ~3000) come from levels with almost no claims; they are reported as WARN and the component prediction check is binding (audit A11).

exploratory_reference._source: Numbers produced during the exploratory session on 2026-10-20 (audit A07, A09). The pack is expected to reproduce them within tol_vs_exploratory; small differences come from unifying band definitions.
